title: Comparing Audiences for a City Health Campaign
instructions: 阅读下面的短文，完成10道题。短文和题目均为原创模拟材料，不是雅思真题。先读题，再读文章。注意倍数与比例表达、比较结构以及过去和现在数据的时态选择。
passage:
A city health team wants more people to walk to work. Last year, the team tested three campaign ideas with three different groups. The results are in the table below.

Table: Campaign test results (simulated data)

| Group | Main message | People who saw the message | People who walked more |
|-------|--------------|----------------------------|------------------------|
| A: Office workers | 'Walk 20 minutes a day' | 1,000 | 250 |
| B: Parents | 'Walk your children to school' | 800 | 320 |
| C: Older adults | 'Walk with a friend' | 600 | 210 |

Group B had the highest proportion of people who walked more. In Group B, 40% of people walked more. In Group A, the figure was 25%. So the proportion in Group B was 1.6 times as high as the proportion in Group A. Group C's proportion was 35%, which was higher than Group A's but lower than Group B's.

The team also looked at the number of people who walked more. Group A had 250 people, Group B had 320, and Group C had 210. Group B had the largest number, but the difference between Group A and Group B was only 70 people. The team noted that Group A's message reached more people (1,000) than Group B's message (800), but fewer people in Group A changed their behaviour. This shows that reaching a large audience does not always lead to more behaviour change. The message itself and how well it fits the audience may matter more. For example, parents may find it easy to walk their children to school because it fits their daily routine, while office workers may need a different reason to walk.

This year, the team is running a new campaign. They are using the message 'Walk with a friend' for all three groups. They believe this message will work well because it was the most effective message for older adults last year. However, they are not sure if it will work for office workers. The team is now collecting new data. They will compare this year's proportions with last year's proportions. They expect the proportion of office workers who walk more to rise from 25% to about 30%. They also expect the number of parents who walk more to stay about the same.

The team says that a message can work well for one group but not for another. They advise campaign planners to test messages with different audiences before using them city-wide. Testing helps planners see which messages work best for each audience. This can save time and money and make campaigns more effective. It also helps avoid wasting resources on messages that do not connect with a particular group.

grammar.title: 倍数与比例表达；比较结构；过去和现在数据的时态选择
grammar.explanation: 英语中表达倍数常用“A is X times as high as B”或“A is X times higher than B”。比例用“the proportion of ...”。比较结构用“more/less/fewer ... than”或“the highest/lowest”。描述过去的数据用一般过去时（如was, had），描述现在正在进行的活动用现在进行时（如is running, are collecting），描述预期用一般将来时（如will compare）。
grammar.example: So the proportion in Group B was 1.6 times as high as the proportion in Group A.

questions.prompt: The number of students in Class A is 30. The number in Class B is 60. So the number in Class B is ______ times as high as the number in Class A.
questions.explanation: 60是30的两倍，所以用2 times as high as。
questions.evidence: So the proportion in Group B was 1.6 times as high as the proportion in Group A.

questions.prompt: Last year, 40% of women and 20% of men joined the club. The proportion of women was ______ the proportion of men.
questions.explanation: 倍数表达用twice as high as，表示“是……的两倍”。
questions.evidence: So the proportion in Group B was 1.6 times as high as the proportion in Group A.

questions.evidence: Group A's message reached more people (1,000) than Group B's message (800).
